objective: Require every tensor-basis implementation to declare its anisotropy and strain-rate conventions and to reproduce Pope's own worked limit case before its coefficients are compared to anything
rationale: Both papers are now READ IN FULL and the ten tensors are identical between them, term for term, so the transcription is checked against two independent printings. The object they multiply is not identical. Pope normalises the anisotropy as the Reynolds stress over k less two thirds of the identity; Ling's own text prints it over twice k less one third. They differ by exactly a factor of two, verified to zero residual, so a coefficient fitted against one is half the other for the same flow and must never be compared to the coefficients Pope prints in his equation 4.3 without it. Worse, and this is the part that cannot be patched afterwards, the strain-rate convention is not printed at all. Ling states only that S and R were non-dimensionalized using the turbulent kinetic energy k and the turbulent dissipation rate as suggested by Pope; there is no equation defining either tensor anywhere in the manuscript and no explicit factor, so Pope's one half in his equations 3.2 and 3.3 has to be assumed rather than read. That assumption is not small, because Pope's tensors are of mixed degree in the strain and rotation rates. Dropping the one half scales the ten tensors by 2, 4, 4, 4, 8, 8, 16, 16, 16 and 32 respectively and the five invariants, which are the model's own input features, by 4, 4, 8, 8 and 16. A convention error is therefore not one constant a fitted coefficient absorbs: it is a different factor on each of the ten coefficients and a simultaneous rescaling of every input the model reads, and a model trained under one convention and evaluated under the other is wrong in a way no single number repairs. This is catchable at zero compute, because Pope's section 5 prints five component expressions for a simple shear flow that any correct implementation reproduces with no free parameter to hide an error in, and this lab's transcription already does so to four parts in ten thousand million million.
gate: Every tensor-basis implementation in the repository declares its anisotropy normalisation and its strain-rate convention in one named place, and a test asserts it reproduces the five component expressions Pope prints on page 336
cost_basis: estimate; a declaration and a unit test, no solver
expected_knowledge_gain: A factor of two between a published coefficient and ours is indistinguishable from a modelling result until somebody writes the convention down
citations: Pope, JFM 72 331 to 340, 1975, equations 3.1 to 3.3 and section 5 p. 336, READ IN FULL 2026-08-02
Ling, Kurzawski & Templeton, SAND2016-7345J, manuscript p. 6, equations 1 and 2, READ IN FULL
in_sample_verdict: Not applicable. No training data of any kind; the test is algebra on a synthetic simple-shear gradient and compares against expressions printed in the paper.
